messages:
maya: noticing a weird pattern — some GPU nodes at 100% but overall cluster utilization shows a lot of idle slots :confused:
sam: can you paste the scheduler logs?
maya: grabbing them now, looks like a bunch of small requests are lining up behind one long-running batch, head-of-line blocking maybe
li: hmm, did admission-controller apply the new per-worker rate limit yesterday? we flipped it to adaptive mode at 02:00 UTC
maya: here are a couple of lines from the scheduler log:
```
2026-11-12T02:14:03Z scheduler DEBUG pick_worker selected=worker-42 queue_len=1 task_id=abc123
2026-11-12T02:14:04Z worker-42 RUNNING task=longgen-req seq=0/2048 gpu_mem=98% kv_cache=locked
2026-11-12T02:14:05Z scheduler DEBUG head_wait detected head_task=longgen-req blocked_by_rate_limit true
2026-11-12T02:14:07Z scheduler DEBUG admission token_granted=0 tokens_available=0
2026-11-12T02:14:09Z scheduler DEBUG pick_worker selected=worker-42 queue_len=5
```
sam: that `tokens_available=0` is the admission controller giving up on other tasks while one GPU is saturated
oliver: sounds like a thundering-herd: many short jobs all routed to workers that are pinned by a single long job, admission doesn't preempt or reassign
li: possibly related to the new backpressure algorithm we shipped — it uses last-assigned-worker affinity to reduce KV cache misses, but affinity + strict token bucket can cause HOL blocking
maya: yes, affinity reduces cache thrash but if a long run pins the worker it prevents others from using spare GPUs, so cluster-level utilization becomes skewed
infra-bot: Incident 2026-11-12-T02:20 created: "Scheduler admission leading to head-of-line blocking" assigned to eng-infra
sam: quick mitigation: disable affinity for requests with seq_len < 64 and allow scheduler to spread small requests across workers
li: or increase token bucket refill rate temporarily while we investigate patterns, but that risks more KV cache misses and slightly higher latency for long tasks
oliver: can we detect long-running tasks and proactively shard their followers? like mark worker-42 as "busy-long" so scheduler will avoid assigning short jobs there
maya: good idea. also add a metric: per-worker "blocked_by_head" that increments when pick_worker sees queue_len>0 and tokens_available==0
sam: I'll open a short PR to add the metric + a soft-avoid flag. In the meantime, rolling back the affinity change to yesterday's config might be safest for production
li: logging suggestion: log `affinity=true/false` and `task_priority` in pick_worker so we can correlate quickly in dashboards
maya: created a rollback runbook in #eng-infra-runbooks, link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/scheduler-affinity-rollback
oliver: pinging oncall infra to run mitigation now — @sam can you trigger the config rollback and bump token refill?
sam: on it, rolling rollback now. patch id: rwd/sched/rollback/8721
infra-bot: deploy started rwd-scheduler v3.14.5 -> canaries
li: post-rollback, let's watch per-region queue lengths. we saw the Europe region especially hit hard because of burst from a single customer job
maya: note for postmortem: include cost analysis — during the incident we had 3x burst in preemptible GPU minutes because requests were queuing and owner retried on other regions
sam: agreed. also add a test to the scheduler sim that models long-tail durations + affinity to catch HOL regressions
oliver: thanks folks. if rollback stabilizes, we'll schedule proper fix: affinity heuristics + detection for long-running locks. :thumbsup:
maya: rollback done, metrics starting to converge. I'll keep monitoring and will update incident thread if anything flares up
sam: nice. follow-up actions: 1) metric + flag PR 2) sim test 3) config for short-request affinity disable 4) postmortem with cost impact
li: assigning owners: sam(1), maya(2), oliver(3) — will draft the postmortem
maya: closing loop — cluster utilization equalizing now, but keeping incident open for 24h to validate
oliver: thanks all :shipit:
